rows: Mean CFO / net profit -111% over 5 years
5 FLAG / 4 WATCH across 16 accounting tests; LojikX™ Consistency Score 35/100

sections.heading: Flagged items in detail
paragraphs: CFO vs. Net Income Conversion: Operating cash flow converted -111% of reported net profit. Profit is running ahead of cash generation, which points to working-capital or accrual quality issues.
FCF Generation Consistency: Free cash flow was positive in 0 of the last 5 reported years. Repeated FCF deficits mean growth is being funded by the balance sheet rather than by the business.
Debt-to-Equity Trajectory: Leverage moved from 0.99x to 2.20x equity. Leverage is high enough to transmit an earnings shock directly into equity value.
Current Ratio Liquidity: Current assets cover current liabilities 1.04 times. Liquidity is tight relative to short-term obligations.
ROE vs. ROCE Quality: Return on capital employed of 8.0% with ROE of 10.0% is close to or below the cost of capital, so growth destroys rather than creates value.
Working Capital Cycle (DSO / DIO): The cash conversion cycle absorbs 108 days of working capital. A long cycle ties up cash and makes growth expensive to fund.
Earnings Volatility Check: Earnings per share fell in 3 of the last 4 years with a growth standard deviation of 29 points. Earnings are erratic, which argues for a wider margin of safety.
Interest Coverage Safety: Operating profit covers interest 2.4 times. Coverage is thin enough that a profit dip would pressure debt service.
Book Value Compounding: Book value per share compounded 7.3% annually. Retained earnings are not translating into balance-sheet growth.

Auditor & Governance Cleanliness: Aggregating the accounting evidence: 5 hard red flags and 4 watch items, with a LojikX™ Consistency Score of 35/100. The pattern of flags warrants a closer read of the auditor notes and related-party disclosures.
